chunks: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he performed wudu (ablution), would not let anyone pour water over him. So it was said to him, “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why do you not let them pour water over you?” Then he said:
I do not like to associate anyone in my salat (prayer).
And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord.”

key_terms.أُشْرِكَ: to associate or involve another in worship
key_terms.صَلَاتِي: my salat (prayer), meaning the act of worship connected with wudu
key_terms.عَمَلًا صَالِحًا: a righteous deed done properly and sincerely

ai.seo_question: Why did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام refuse to let others pour water for his wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the practice of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in personally carrying out wudu (ablution) without another person pouring the water for him. It connects this practice to sincerity in worship, supported by the Qur’anic teaching that righteous deeds must be done without associating anyone in the worship of Allah.
